one_liner: 3D FFT layer for sparse (spherical-cutoff) frequency data that skips empty columns before calling FFTW/MKL/cuFFT/rocFFT; no published speedup.
what_it_does: Computes forward and backward 3D C2C, R2C and C2R transforms where the frequency-domain side is a sparse list of (x, y, z) index triplets, as produced by a plane-wave energy cutoff in electronic-structure codes, and the space-domain side is a dense grid. The API is not FFTW-like: you build a Grid (pre-allocated buffers up to a maximum size, optionally bound to an MPI communicator and a GPU) and create Transform handles from it with the index list, then call backward()/forward() with host or GPU pointers; C and Fortran interfaces mirror the C++ classes. Distributed runs use slab decomposition in space and z-pencil (z-column) decomposition in frequency, with all elements of a z-column on one rank.
how_it_is_fast: Pruned 3D FFT by dimension: on the host it runs the batched 1D z-transforms only over the z-columns that hold data (decompress, z-FFT, transpose), then the y-transforms only for x indices that own a column (Transform1DVerticalHost with uniqueXIndices), and full x-transforms last, so zero columns and empty y-lines are never touched. For R2C/C2R it exploits Hermitian symmetry so only half the columns (plus the non-redundant half of the x=0 plane) are needed. The z-to-xy redistribution is an MPI all-to-all (Alltoall, Alltoallv or Alltoallw variants, optionally exchanging doubles as floats to halve traffic), and Grid buffers are reused across transforms; all 1D/2D kernels are FFTW, MKL, ARMPL, NVPL, cuFFT or rocFFT plans, not SpFFT's own.
when_to_use: Plane-wave DFT or similar codes where frequency data is a sphere inside a cube, so most z-columns are empty (this is what SIRIUS, and through it Quantum ESPRESSO and CP2K, use it for).
Repeated transforms of the same sparsity pattern, where the cost of building the Grid/Transform (FFTW planning, index setup) is amortized over many calls.
MPI-distributed 3D grids that already use z-column ownership per rank, on CPU or on NVIDIA (CUDA 11+) or AMD (ROCm 5+) GPUs, with optional GPU-aware MPI.
Codes that need one interface for host and GPU execution and C/Fortran bindings.
when_not_to_use: Dense frequency data or 2D problems: there is nothing to prune, and a third-party test (cuSpFFT course project, RTX 4090, single precision, full R2C output set) measured SpFFT at 0.74x, 0.41x and 0.17x the speed of plain dense cuFFT with 1.3-2.3x more device memory; it ran out of memory on a 52,329^2 case.
When you need evidence of a speedup: the repo publishes no timings against FFTW, MKL or cuFFT, and tests/programs/benchmark.cpp times only SpFFT itself.
Sparsity in the space domain (sparse inputs to a forward transform) or arbitrary non-column patterns: only frequency-side sparsity grouped into complete z-columns is supported.
1D FFTs, non-uniform FFTs, or sizes with large prime factors: it only does 3D transforms and inherits the backend's speed on sizes not of the form 2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d.
Projects that need a multi-GPU single transform: each Grid/Transform is tied to one GPU.

integration.form: shared lib (static with SPFFT_STATIC=ON); CMake build, conda-forge package
integration.dependencies: a library with the FFTW 3.x interface (FFTW3, Intel MKL, ARM Performance Libraries or NVPL); optional MPI, OpenMP, CUDA 11+ (cuFFT) or ROCm 5+ (rocFFT/hipFFT)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; GCC 7+, Clang 5+ or ICC 19+; CMake 3.18 (3.21 for ROCm)
integration.platforms: Linux HPC targets: x86-64 and Arm CPUs, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs; other platforms not documented
integration.thread_safety: Grid/Transform creation is thread-safe only if no other FFTW calls run concurrently (and MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE when distributed); execution is thread-safe when each thread uses its own Grid and Transform. Creation and execution are collective over all MPI ranks.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it calls FFTW/MKL/cuFFT/rocFFT underneath, but the caller must supply the sparse index triplets and use the Grid/Transform API, so it replaces a hand-rolled pruned 3D FFT rather than an fftw_plan_dft_3d call

gotchas: Index layout rules: all elements of one z-column must be on the same rank, R2C inputs need x in [0, n/2], and the docs say the order and rank distribution of z-columns strongly affects speed (continuous in y for host, in x for GPU).
Normalization is only applied on forward transforms (1/(Nx*Ny*Nz)); backward is never scaled.

Bug history in released versions: wrong results with 2 OpenMPI ranks (issue #51, labelled Bug/Wrong Results, closed January 2022), ROCm Release builds left debug device_synchronize() on (fixed in 1.1.0), C/Fortran multi-transform segfault (fixed in 1.1.1), and an array size mismatch for local transforms fixed in PR #65 (2025-07-25) after the last release v1.1.1.
Creating Grids/Transforms inside an OpenMP parallel region crashed in FFTW planning (issue #32); create them outside the region.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SpFFT over heFFTe (dense distributed 3D FFT) when your frequency data is a plane-wave cutoff sphere and you want the empty columns skipped for you. cuSpFFT solves a different problem (binary-sparse 2D inputs on one GPU) and beat SpFFT only in an off-design test where SpFFT was given a full output set.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing measured: the repository, its docs and its benchmark program make no speed claim and contain no comparison against FFTW, MKL, cuFFT or rocFFT. The only third-party numbers found (cuSpFFT README, RTX 4090, single precision, 2D full-output use) show SpFFT slower than dense cuFFT, which is outside SpFFT's sparse 3D design point.
status_note: Stale but maintained at a low rate: last release v1.1.1 (2025-01-19) and last commit 2025-07-25; BSD-3-Clause, packaged on conda-forge and a required dependency of SIRIUS, so it is exercised in production electronic-structure codes.
